Announced via a teaser we covered last week, DJI shares that the official premiere of its new Osmo Pocket 4P gimbal camera is at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival this week\. This follow-up to the popular DJI Osmo Pocket 4 is a bigger, more powerful option with dual cameras and higher cinematic capabilities\.

But does the DJI Osmo Pocket 4P offer enough high-end cinema specs and features to actually be an option for big-screen filmmakers, even if they are indie or studio? Let’s take a look at the new Osmo Pocket 4P from DJI and explore what it has to offer, thanks to this Cannes premiere\.

---

### DJI Osmo Pocket 4P Premiere

It might be a marketing gimmick, of course, but DJI’s decision to premiere the new Osmo Pocket 4P at the Cannes Film Festival in France is pretty on-the-nose for how the company wants to position this new pocket-sized gimbal camera with its cinematic ambitions\.

And from this film festival debut, we have more to share about what makes the Osmo Pocket 4P a unique, more cinematically capable follow-up to the previous Osmo Pocket 4 model\. The Pocket 4P is set to build on the company’s top-end camera gimbal technology, as seen in the Ronin 4D, as well as its popular \(yet blacklisted\) drones\.

The DJI Osmo Pocket 4P will feature what the company calls a “cinematic-level dynamic range for rich tonal depth,” along with 10-bit D-Log2 color performance\. As you might expect, the pocket-gimbal camera will also feature advanced stabilization, all packed into a quite small and easy-to-transfer form factor\.

Credit: DJI

### Cinematic Ambitions

Still, even with this Cannes premiere, we don’t have all the full specs and features for this new pocket gimbal camera outlined just yet\. We do have plenty of quotes from the company that further attempt to tie its release to its push into higher-end productions and to bring more cinematic quality overall to its products\.

“At Cannes, the Osmo Pocket 4P is already being explored by filmmakers, documentary creators, and visual storytellers seeking agile, high-quality production tools\. Its compact form, paired with cinematic imaging performance, positions it as a compelling companion for independent filmmakers and a powerful storytelling device for documentary work\. The debut at Cannes reinforces the idea that cinematic storytelling is no longer confined to large-scale rigs, but can now exist in a device small enough to carry anywhere\.” - DJI

The company continues to promise that the Osmo Pocket 4P marks a new direction for it to continue developing products aimed at inspiring “a new generation of mobile-first filmmakers,” and that it will continue to introduce new products across its gimbals, drones, audio, and stabilization solutions\.

Credit: DJI

### Price and Availability

As mentioned above, we still don’t have full details on price and availability just yet\. And, as has been the case with many new DJI products as of late, we’re also not sure if the Osmo Pocket 4P will even be available in the US at launch\. So, for those details, stay tuned for more info soon\.

Disney and Osmo have announced the launch of the new Osmo Super Studio featuring Mickey Mouse’s first reflective animation experience\. This award winning and innovative system allows kids to physically draw Mickey and his iconic pals, who then come to life on screen via Osmo’s Reflective AI\.

Here are the details:

Classroom walls and refrigerators are home to some of the most beloved drawings in the world and stand as crayon and scented-marker tributes to every child’s natural love of telling stories with pictures\. Today, Osmo, the award-winning system that sparked a new category of seamless digital and hands-on play for the iPad, teams up with Disney to bring those drawings to life in stories with Osmo Super Studio featuring Disney’s Mickey Mouse & Friends\.

Drawing is a critical childhood activity linked to social and emotional development, according to research from the National Endowment for Arts\. It’s also a way to ignite the imagination and create new worlds with beloved friends\. Now, Osmo is collaborating with Disney to bring Mickey Mouse, Minnie Mouse, Donald, Daisy and all their pals to life in a magical new way\. You can also provide your children with a drawing device to further fuel their artistic abilities\.

Iconic Disney Characters Come to Life Kids guide the story in Osmo Super Studio by supplying Mickey Mouse and Friends with realworld drawings that are “pulled” into the story’s digital world and by answering yes or no questions\. It boosts kids’ creativity as they help to shape the storyline with whatever they imagine belongs in the tale\. As the story progresses, characters ask for tools, toys, scenery and snacks to bring into their world\. When kids are asked to draw Daisy they have the freedom to draw her as they see her – or how they’d like to see her – with a bow or an astronaut helmet – the only limit is a child’s imagination\.

“The power of computer vision and AI can bring a child’s imagination to life in new and innovative ways,” said Pramod Sharma, CEO and co-founder of Osmo\. “This first-of-its-kind Reflective Animation experience bridges the world populated by the characters beloved by children of all ages with the creativity and artistic expression\.”

Draw ‘Em How You See ‘Em Osmo’s proprietary Reflective AI technology, that allows the iPad’s camera to “see” physical objects in front of it, is at the heart of the world’s first Reflective Animation experience that gives kids a blank canvas to express themselves through story and by drawing their favorite Disney characters how they see them: any color, any size, any shape\.

Osmo Super Studio combines the fun of Disney characters and storytelling with the power of art and self-expression so kids can bring Mickey Mouse to life as they see him in their imaginations\.

Osmo Super Studio is suggested for kids ages 5 and up and is available as an add-on to existing Osmo sets for $19\. Those new to Osmo can buy the Super Studio Kit that includes an Osmo iPad Base for $79\.

Get your copy of Osmo Super Studio today at PlayOsmo\.com and Amazon\.com, as well as Target and Best Buy\.

Super Studio is the eleventh innovative experience to come to Osmo’s universe\. Recently named one of the most innovative companies in 2017 by Fast Company and Osmo is now going beyond the iPad with the Osmo iPhone Base\.

DJI Philippines unveiled the Osmo 360, its first 360-degree action camera, in a glamorous launch event at Xylo at the Palace, Taguig City, last August 23, 2025\. Content creators, vloggers, and tech experts witnessed how DJI is entering the 360 camera market with a compact yet advanced device designed for immersive storytelling\.

The Osmo 360 introduces a 1-inch square HDR sensor that delivers crisp, vivid images with 25% more sensor utilization compared to traditional rectangular sensors\. It shoots 8K/50fps 360 video, records continuously for 100 minutes at 8K/30fps, and captures up to 120-megapixel 360 photos\. Its large pixel size ensures better low-light performance and higher dynamic range\.

Beyond imaging, the Osmo 360 offers practical features for creators\. Users can switch between front and rear lenses without stopping recording\. A single-lens mode turns it into an action camera, while boost mode expands the view to 170 degrees at 4K/120fps\. With 105 GB of built-in storage and a lightweight body, it is ideal for creators on the go\.

Durability is also a highlight\. The Osmo 360 withstands extreme weather and records up to 1\.5 hours in freezing conditions\. The Battery Extension Rod recharges the camera to 50% in just 12 minutes\. Additional smart features include HorizonSteady, RockSteady stabilization, gesture and voice control, invisible selfie stick, and slow-motion capture\.

The Osmo 360 Standard Combo is priced at P24,490, while the Adventure Combo is priced at P30,990, each packed with accessories\. Both are available in DJI stores, major malls nationwide, and online platforms\.

With Osmo 360, DJI Philippines enters a new era of immersive content creation, offering an all-in-one adventure companion for filmmakers, vloggers, and storytellers\.

# DJI Osmo 360 II Officially Launches Tomorrow

The DJI Osmo 360 II is officially set to launch on August 7, 2026, marking an important moment in the 360-camera market\. As highlighted by Tech Court, this release introduces several confirmed features, including a **2,150 mAh battery for extended recording sessions** and **27W USB-C fast charging** to minimize downtime\. Additionally, the inclusion of user-replaceable lenses enhances durability, making the device more practical for intensive use\. These updates position the Osmo 360 II as a versatile option for creators seeking reliability and convenience in their workflows\.

Explore how the Osmo 360 II compares to its closest competitor, the Insta360 X6, which is also launching this week\. Gain insight into the specific upgrades DJI has made to image processing, stabilization and overall usability\. You’ll also learn about the broader implications of this dual launch for the 360-camera market, particularly in areas like low-light performance, battery efficiency and design\. This announcement offers a clear look at what creators can expect from the next generation of immersive content capture\.

## What’s New with the DJI Osmo 360 II?

**TL;DR Key Takeaways :**

- DJI has officially announced the Osmo 360 II, launching on August 7, 2026, with key upgrades like extended battery life, faster charging and improved image processing\.
- Insta360 is set to release its X6 model simultaneously, featuring 8K recording, 10-bit color and enhanced low-light performance, creating direct competition with DJI\.
- The Osmo 360 II introduces user-replaceable lenses and advancements in stabilization and color science, catering to both casual users and professionals\.
- The Insta360 X6 emphasizes portability, a sleek design and innovative features like “Pure Video” technology for superior low-light footage\.
- The rivalry between DJI and Insta360 reflects rapid innovation in the 360-camera market, empowering creators with versatile tools for immersive storytelling and professional-grade content creation\.

The DJI Osmo 360 II introduces a range of upgrades aimed at improving both performance and usability\. These enhancements are designed to cater to the needs of casual users and professionals alike, making sure a versatile tool for various creative applications\. Key features include:

- **Extended Battery Life:** Equipped with a larger 2,150 mAh battery, the Osmo 360 II offers longer recording sessions, minimizing interruptions caused by frequent recharging\.
- **Faster Charging:** The inclusion of 27W USB-C charging technology significantly reduces downtime, allowing users to quickly resume their work\.
- **User-Replaceable Lenses:** This practical feature makes it easier to address lens damage, especially during intensive or outdoor shoots, enhancing the camera’s durability and longevity\.
- **Improved Image Processing:** DJI has hinted at advancements in stabilization, color science and image clarity, making sure smoother footage and richer visuals even in challenging environments\.

While DJI has kept some details under wraps, these confirmed features suggest that the Osmo 360 II is designed to deliver reliability, quality and convenience, making it a strong contender in the 360-camera market\.

## Insta360 X6: A Worthy Competitor

Insta360 is not backing down from the competition\. The upcoming **X6 model** has generated significant excitement, with rumors pointing to several innovative features that could redefine user expectations\. Anticipated highlights include:

- **8K Recording:** The X6 is expected to support 8K video at up to 50fps, providing creators with exceptional detail and clarity\.
- **10-Bit Color:** Enhanced tonal depth and color accuracy will appeal to professionals who prioritize visual fidelity in their projects\.
- **Low-Light Performance:** Insta360’s proprietary “Pure Video” technology is designed to deliver clearer and sharper footage in dimly lit environments\.
- **Compact Design and Replaceable Lenses:** A portable form factor combined with a user-friendly lens replacement system makes the X6 ideal for creators on the go\.
- **New Aesthetic Options:** A sleek white color variant adds a modern and stylish touch to the X6’s design, appealing to users who value both form and function\.

These features indicate that Insta360 is targeting creators who demand both technical excellence and aesthetic appeal, making sure the X6 stands out as a versatile and powerful tool\.

With both DJI and Insta360 striving to set new standards, the tools available to creators are becoming more powerful and versatile than ever\. # DJI Osmo 360 II Pre-Orders Open in China, Launch August 13

**DJI** opened pre-orders for the **Osmo 360 II** in China on Thursday, August 7, at 8:00 pm Beijing time, and confirmed the camera will launch on August 13 at 8:00 pm local time\. The reservation page went live three weeks after the first prototype photos leaked, and it puts a hard date on the second generation of a 360 camera that sold out repeatedly in its first run\. The rest of the world waits, again\.

## DJI Confirms the Date and Shows the Design

The launch is official and dated: August 13 at 8:00 pm China time, which is 12:00 UTC and 8:00 am on the US East Coast, with reservations already open on DJI’s Chinese storefront ahead of the event\. That much comes from DJI itself, not from the rumor mill\.

**Notebookcheck** notes the reservation system works more like a purchase reminder than a true pre-order with money down\. You sign up, DJI pings you when the button goes live\. The teaser also revealed the camera’s design, which stays close to the first generation’s square-sensor layout\.

Pricing has not been announced for any market\. DJI has said nothing official about availability outside China either\. Based on how the company has rolled out recent launches, coverage across the tech press expects a phased global announcement later this month, but that is an expectation built on DJI’s habits, not on a statement\.

## Replaceable Lenses Answer the Loudest Complaint

The single most requested fix appears to have made it into the new camera: lenses you can swap yourself when they scratch\. On the first Osmo 360, a scratched lens meant a service ticket or a dead camera, because the glass was not user-replaceable, and 360 cameras live with their lenses exposed on both faces\.

Photo credit: DJI

**The New Camera**, which first reported the Chinese pre-order window, calls the non-replaceable lenses the biggest problem of the first generation\. Anyone who mounted one on a helmet or a drone and came home with a scarred front element already knows why\.

A 360 camera without lens protection is a design contradiction\. The whole point of the format is sticking the camera where the action is, and the action is exactly where glass gets hurt\. If the swappable lens system holds up in practice, this one change matters more to working creators than any resolution bump\.

## Leaked Specs Point to 8K60 and a Bigger Battery

Everything below comes from leaks and pre-launch reporting rather than a DJI spec sheet, so treat the numbers as expected rather than confirmed\. The consistent picture across the prototype coverage DroneXL published in July and the current wave of reports: 8K video at 60 frames per second, up from 8K50 on the original, and a 2,150 mAh battery replacing the 1,950 mAh cell\.

That battery math deserves a closer look than the headline suggests\. The cell grows about 10 percent, but the processing needed to push 8K60 does not come free\. A bigger battery feeding hungrier silicon can leave real-world recording time flat or even shorter\. Whether the Osmo 360 II actually records longer than its predecessor is an open question the spec sheet will not settle\. Reviewers with production units will\.

The reports also point to 27W USB-C fast charging, Wi-Fi 6, and NFC support\. The NFC addition is the quietly practical one: tap the camera against your phone to pair and pull files, instead of the usual app-and-password dance\. For creators moving 8K 360 files in the field, transfer speed is not a luxury spec\.

## The US Market Watches Another China-First Launch

DJI launching a flagship camera in China while American buyers refresh the page is now a pattern, not an event\. The original Osmo 360 launched in July 2025 with no US sale, and the Osmo Pocket 4P repeated the script last week: global launch, no US price, no US date\.

The reason sits in Washington, not Shenzhen\. The December 2025 national security determination cut off new equipment authorizations for DJI hardware, and a camera that cannot get authorized cannot be sold\. The New Camera reports the Osmo 360 II cleared its FCC authorization on December 21, 2025, one day before that determination took effect, which would make it legally eligible for US sale\. DroneXL has not independently confirmed that filing date\.

If the timing claim holds, the Osmo 360 II would be in a stranger position than the Pocket 4P: a brand-new DJI camera that squeaked through the door as it closed\. Watch the August 13 launch and the announcements DJI makes in the weeks after it for whether a US price appears\.

## DroneXL’s Take

The 360 category’s real bottleneck is not in the camera\. It is in the edit\. Every 360 camera sold ships with a promise that you can frame the shot after you live the moment, and most buyers never get there, because reframing 8K spherical footage is a skill nobody taught them\. They shoot in every direction, export something flat and overcompressed with a default preset, and quietly go back to a regular action camera\.

I will say what I have said before: I do not fully get 360 cameras\. When I tried the format, it was fun for exactly one kind of shot\. After 28 years working behind cameras, I know the difference between a tool that changes your work and a tool that demos well in a store\.

That is why the smartest money DJI could spend on this launch is not on the sensor\. It is on creators who teach the software\. Fund the people showing beginners how to reframe in DJI Studio in a way that is creative and easy, because the camera’s output is only as good as the edit the owner can actually produce\. Swappable lenses fix the hardware complaint\. Nobody has fixed the education gap yet\.

The first real-world footage lands after August 13\. That is when we find out if the second generation earns the wait\.

# DJI Osmo 360 II teased alongside possible August 13 launch

\(Image credit: DJI\)

A not-so mysterious teaser has appeared on the DJI website that is clearly regarding the much-anticipated DJI Osmo 360 II\. The page, which is only available if your region is set to Hong Kong, is entitled “All Angles\. All Epic\.” Along with a date of August 13 2026, 12PM GMT\.

This appears to contradict other teasers, with a second teaser posted on DJI’s Instagram, stating: “DJI Osmo 360 II will be available for pre-order starting at 8:00PM on August 7th\.” \(translated using Google Lens\)\. This would appear to corroborate another post that surfaced on Chinese social media and was reported on by **Asobinet** stating that the 360 camera would be “unveiled on August 7th\.” However, as of yet, I haven’t seen any more information regarding the 360 camera’s launch\.\.\.

The second Instagram teaser is a showreel of 360 footage, captured on the DJI Osmo 360 II, showing POV shots of mountain biking, dancing, skiing and more\. When the teaser ends, it simply states: “Coming soon”\.

A slightly earlier teaser was released, which features the same video present on DJI’s Hong Kong website\. It starts with a top-down view of a square sensor, with the camera pulling back to reveal a lens and then the top of the camera itself\. A fisheye lens is then overlaid over the top\.

DJI hasn’t yet revealed any specs\. However, I’m expecting some juicy upgrades from the Osmo 360’s already very impressive 8K / 50p and 6K / 60p video, 120MP panoramic stills, and 105GB available storage\. It would appear that a few commenters are having fun coming up with some entirely unachievable specs, with one ‘hoping for’ “24k resolution, 2000fps open gate global shutter”\.

News of the Osmo 360 II comes at a time when both DJI and its customer base face growing uncertainty when it comes to product availability in the US\. Government restrictions targeting Chinese-made drones are well documented, but other DJI products have faced scrutiny, including the new DJI Osmo Pocket 4 and 4P\. As such, it seems likely the Osmo 360 II will not be available in the US at launch\.

Still, the DJI Osmo 360 II is releasing elsewhere and DJI’s teasers will have definitely put its competitors on notice\. As soon as we know more about this impending release, we’ll be posting about it right here on Digital Camera World\.

# DJI Osmo Pocket 4P Teased With Dual Camera, 3-Axis Gimbal, and Telephoto Camera Features

DJI Osmo Pocket 4P is officially teased with a dual camera, 3-axis gimbal, telephoto camera, and new features expected for creators and vloggers\. The FIlm Alliance/YTScreenshot

DJI has officially teased the DJI Osmo Pocket 4P, giving creators an early look at what could become its most advanced pocket-sized camera yet\.

The teaser confirms one of the biggest rumored upgrades—a dual camera system—while continuing the compact design and 3-axis gimbal stabilization that have made the Osmo Pocket lineup popular with vloggers and filmmakers\.

Although DJI has not shared the complete specifications, the teaser and multiple industry reports suggest the new model will introduce several hardware and imaging improvements\. Among the rumored additions are a dedicated telephoto camera, a larger image sensor, faster recording modes, and upgraded subject tracking\.

As more details emerge, the DJI Osmo Pocket 4P is shaping up to be a versatile camera for creators who want professional-looking footage in a device that easily fits into a pocket\.

## DJI Gives a First Look at the Osmo Pocket 4P

DJI recently released an official teaser highlighting the upcoming DJI Osmo Pocket 4P\. The image reveals a redesigned camera module featuring two lenses instead of the traditional single-camera setup used in previous Osmo Pocket models\.

The company also describes the camera as being built for advanced creators, emphasizing flexible focal lengths and cinematic storytelling\. While the teaser leaves many questions unanswered, it confirms that the next-generation model is focused on expanding creative shooting options without sacrificing portability\.

According to DJI's announcement, additional information will be revealed during the official launch event\.

## Dual Camera Headlines the Biggest Upgrade

The most noticeable addition is the new dual camera system\. Rather than relying on digital zoom, the DJI Osmo Pocket 4P is expected to combine a primary wide-angle camera with a dedicated telephoto camera\.

This design offers several practical benefits for content creators:

- Better framing without moving closer to the subject\.
- Improved portrait shots with a more natural perspective\.
- Higher-quality zoom compared to digital cropping\.
- Greater flexibility for travel and street photography\.
- Easier switching between wide and close-up compositions\.

For users who frequently record videos on the move, having two focal lengths available in a compact camera can reduce the need for carrying extra equipment\.

## Expected DJI Osmo Pocket 4P Features

Although many specifications remain unofficial, reports from reliable industry sources point to several notable upgrades\.

Expected DJI Osmo Pocket 4P features include:

- 1-inch primary image sensor\.
- Dedicated 3x telephoto camera\.
- 4K video recording at up to 240fps\.
- Up to 14 stops of dynamic range\.
- 10-bit D-Log color recording\.
- Hasselblad color tuning\.
- Enhanced ActiveTrack subject tracking\.
- Up to 128GB built-in storage\.
- Flip-out touchscreen display\.
- Faster image processing performance\.

These specifications are based on leaks and early reports\. DJI has not yet confirmed the complete hardware configuration\.

## The 3-Axis Gimbal Remains a Key Feature

Another highlight of the DJI Osmo Pocket 4P is its 3-axis gimbal\. Unlike cameras that depend only on electronic image stabilization, a mechanical gimbal physically compensates for movement across three axes to produce smoother footage\.

This stabilization system makes handheld recording much easier, especially when walking or following moving subjects\. As a result, creators can capture cinematic-looking clips without using a larger external stabilizer\.

The 3-axis gimbal continues to be one of the defining features of the Osmo Pocket series, and many expect DJI to improve its responsiveness and tracking performance on the new model\.

## Telephoto Camera Expands Creative Possibilities

The addition of a dedicated telephoto camera is expected to provide more shooting flexibility than previous generations\.

Instead of enlarging footage digitally, a telephoto lens captures distant subjects with greater clarity while maintaining image quality\. It can also produce a more compressed background, making portraits appear more natural\.

Possible shooting scenarios include:

1. Portrait photography and video\.
1. Wildlife and nature recording\.
1. Sports and live events\.
1. Street photography\.
1. Travel landmarks and architecture\.

Combined with the primary camera, the telephoto lens allows creators to switch between different perspectives without changing equipment\.

## How the DJI Osmo Pocket 4P Could Compare With Earlier Models

While DJI has not published a full comparison, the teaser suggests several upgrades over previous Osmo Pocket cameras\.

Expected improvements include:

- Dual camera instead of a single-camera design\.
- Dedicated telephoto camera for optical zoom\.
- Improved low-light image quality\.
- Enhanced ActiveTrack performance\.
- Faster video recording options\.
- Larger internal storage\.
- More advanced color processing\.

If these reports prove accurate, the DJI Osmo Pocket 4P would offer greater versatility while keeping the compact size that made earlier models popular\.

## What Has Been Confirmed and What Is Still Unofficial

At this stage, only a handful of details have been officially confirmed by DJI\.

Officially confirmed:

- Dual camera design\.
- Compact handheld form factor\.
- Creator-focused positioning\.
- Continued use of a 3-axis gimbal\.

Still based on leaks and reports:

- 1-inch image sensor\.
- 3x telephoto camera\.
- 4K 240fps recording\.
- Internal storage capacity\.
- Battery life\.
- Price\.
- Official release date\.

More information is expected once DJI announces the camera in full\.

## Early Reports Point to a Strong Upgrade for Creators

The official teaser has already confirmed that the DJI Osmo Pocket 4P will introduce one of the biggest hardware changes in the history of the Osmo Pocket lineup\. The combination of a dual camera, a dedicated telephoto camera, and the signature 3-axis gimbal suggests that DJI is expanding the camera's capabilities while preserving its portable design\.

Additional specifications remain unconfirmed, but early reports indicate improvements in video quality, stabilization, storage, and subject tracking\. As DJI reveals more information during the official launch, creators will have a clearer picture of how the DJI Osmo Pocket 4P compares with previous models and what new features it brings to handheld content creation\.

Industry reports from Engadget first highlighted DJI's official teaser and several leaked specifications surrounding the camera\. Separate coverage from News\.com\.au also discussed expected imaging improvements and creator-focused upgrades based on early hands-on information\. Meanwhile, DJI's official teaser provides the only confirmed details available before the full product announcement\.

## Frequently Asked Questions

# DJI Osmo 360 II Launches With 8K60 And No American Price

**DJI** put the **Osmo 360 II** on sale in China on Thursday, August 13, at 8:00 pm Beijing time, pricing the standard package at 3,299 yuan, about $460\. The second generation of DJI’s panoramic camera records native 8K video at 60 frames per second, swaps its lenses by hand, and ships with 105GB of internal storage\. The company’s US store, checked minutes after the reveal, returns a 404 page\.

## The Launch Sheet Confirms The Leaks And Adds The Fine Print

The Osmo 360 II records native panoramic video at 7680 by 3840 pixels from 24 to 60 frames per second, meters up to 14\.5 stops of dynamic range by DJI’s lab numbers, and takes user-replaceable lenses hardened with an ion sputtering coating, according to the specifications DJI published at launch\.

A week of pre-launch reporting called the headline features correctly\. When DroneXL covered the Chinese pre-order window on August 7, the expected package was 8K60 and swappable lenses\. Both held up\.

DJI's launch materials lead with the sensor: 1-inch-class panoramic imaging and native 8K60 video\. Photo credit: DJI

The fine print is where the launch sheet earns a read\. The night mode, listed as AI Super Night Scene 2\.0 in DJI’s Chinese materials, now records at up to 8K60\. In the D-Log M color profile, dynamic range tops out at a rated 13\.5 stops\.

Slow motion gets two lanes\. Panorama mode captures 4K at 240fps for 8x slow motion, and **DJI Studio** can stretch native 8K60 footage through AI frame interpolation into what DJI rates as the equivalent of 8K480, a trick reserved for Apple’s M-series Macs\.

A subject-tracking mode keeps a person centered in the spherical frame and exports a flat 4K30 video automatically through the **DJI Mimo** app or DJI Studio\. Single-lens mode reaches 4K120 in ultra-wide, and the camera switches lenses mid-recording at up to 4K60 without stopping the file\.

The subject-tracking mode holds a person centered in the spherical frame and exports flat 4K30 video automatically\. Photo credit: DJI

Storage carries over rather than growing: the same 105GB of internal memory the first generation shipped with, plus a microSD slot\. Panoramas record in DJI’s OSV format, flat exports in MP4 HEVC\.

## The Battery Rating Lands Where The Skepticism Pointed

DJI rates the Osmo 360 II at up to 100 minutes of continuous 8K30 panoramic recording, or 120 minutes in its long battery life mode, and that 100-minute 8K30 figure is the same rating the original **Osmo 360** carried at its Chinese launch in July 2025\.

The pre-launch leaks sold a bigger battery as a longer runtime\. DroneXL’s pre-order coverage flagged the catch: a larger cell feeding silicon hungry enough for 8K60 can leave real-world recording time flat\. The launch sheet settles it\. The rating did not move\.

The battery story is swappable rather than sealed\. The camera pairs with a new 2,150 mAh cold-resistant pack, sold separately at 189 yuan, about $26, and rated for -4 F to 113 F \(-20 C to 45 C\)\. It still accepts the older Osmo Action packs at 1,950 and 1,770 mAh\.

That cross-compatibility is the quiet win for anyone already carrying DJI action cameras\. The charger tray in the bag does not care which body the battery feeds\.

## Insta360 Moved First And Priced Higher

The **Insta360 X6** launched 23 hours earlier at $699\.99 in the United States, carrying dual 1/1\.1-inch sensors, native Dolby Vision, and a 2,600 mAh battery rated at 140 minutes of 8K30 recording, numbers aimed squarely at the camera DJI revealed today\.

DroneXL’s coverage of the X6 launch read the date as the real story: two Shenzhen companies shipping flagship 360 cameras 23 hours apart, with exactly one of them able to reach American shelves\.

The China pricing sharpens that picture\. The first Osmo 360 launched at 2,999 yuan in China and $549\.99 in the United States, matching the **Insta360 X5** it chased\. When DroneXL compared those two cameras last August, price parity was DJI’s opening move\.

The second generation adds 300 yuan, a 10 percent bump\. If the China-to-US spread of the first generation held, the Osmo 360 II would land near $600 in America, roughly $100 under the X6\. That math stays hypothetical, because there is no American price to check it against\.

Bundles run from a 3,499 yuan riding kit to a 4,006 yuan diving package, with a 3,999 yuan shooting kit in between\. Chinese buyers also get twelve months of interest-free installments and a year of DJI Care thrown in at launch\.

Bundle pricing on DJI's China store, with a year of DJI Care included at launch\. Photo credit: DJI

## The US Store Answers With A 404

The Osmo 360 II holds a valid **FCC** equipment authorization, granted December 21, 2025, one day before the Covered List cutoff froze new approvals for DJI hardware, yet DJI’s American storefront carries no product page and no US price for the camera it just launched everywhere else\.

I loaded DJI’s US store minutes after the 12:00 UTC reveal\. The page apologizes, promises an auto-redirect in six seconds, and dumps you back on the homepage\. The grant is public record under FCC ID 2ANDR-OQ0022512\. The store does not acknowledge the product exists\.

The pattern around it is consistent\. The **Osmo Pocket 4P** launched globally in July with no US page\. The **Mic Mini 2S** followed on August 4 the same way, and the **O4 Wide Air Unit** skipped America in June\.

DJI’s April brief to the **US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit** counted five drone models and nine handheld products blocked from the US market, with 25 more launches in limbo\. The same filing put lost American revenue near $1\.56 billion this year\. The Osmo 360 II was supposed to be the exception\. Launch day says otherwise\.

## DroneXL’s Take

Earlier this week I wrote that Americans might finally be invited to a DJI launch, because the Osmo 360 II cleared its FCC authorization one day before the Covered List cutoff froze new approvals\. Half of that held up today\. The authorization is real\. The invitation never printed\.

Put this camera next to the Mic Mini 2S and the Pocket 4P, the two launches Americans watched from outside this summer\. Same company\. Same engineers\. Same shelf in every other market\. The thing that separates the legal product from the invisible ones is not technology and it is not security\. It is a filing date\. National security, as currently written, is a calendar\.

The eligible camera and the blocked ones now share the same American outcome anyway, and that should bother both sides of the ban debate\. If the December grant makes the Osmo 360 II legal to sell, then the empty US page is a choice, and every American creator shopping for a 360 camera this month pays $699\.99 for the X6 with no competitor on the shelf beside it\.

Whether DJI converts its paper eligibility into an American price is an open question, not a prediction\. I checked the 404 page one more time before filing this\. Still redirecting\.
